steps.text: Beat cream in a chilled glass or metal bowl with an electric mixer until frothy.
Beat in confectioners' sugar and vanilla, continuing to beat, until soft peaks form.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Whipped Cream
raw_recipe.description: This whipped cream recipe shows you how to whisk heavy cream in an ice-cold bowl with confectioners' sugar to make a sweet cream that holds its shape.

video.description: Ditch the store-bought whipped cream and try this easy, 3-ingredient recipe! In this video, Nicole shows you how to make homemade whipped cream to take your dessert to the next level. To easily make this delicious topping, make sure to chill the mixing bowl beforehand. Using only heavy cream, powdered sugar, and vanilla extract, whip together the ingredients. With a dollop of this whipped cream, it’ll make any dessert taste homemade!

recipeInstructions.text: Beat cream in a chilled glass or metal bowl with an electric mixer until frothy.
Beat in confectioners' sugar and vanilla, continuing to beat, until soft peaks form.

review.reviewBody: Good recipe. Chill mixing bowl and beaters in freezer for 10 minutes before preparing. Also,can experiment with different extracts to get just the right flavor to go with that perfect recipe (rum extract,almond,banana,coconut,maple,coffee)~tried them all :)

Good basic recipe but the instructions are a tad misleading. It says to add sugar and vanilla when the cream becomes frothy, but if you’re using cream that is just cream and DOES NOT have emulsifiers or thickeners added to it (as most store bought heavy creams do) this instruction will not work. You must wait to add sugar and vanilla until the cream thickens and forms soft peaks, otherwise it won’t stiffen up at all. I used raw cream and had trouble when following the recipe as written. So, to correct the recipe: 1. Whip/beat cold cream until soft peaks form 2. Add sugar and vanilla 3. Whip/beat to combine and until stiff peaks form (or desired consistency is reached)

Easy and fast recipe. Doubled the sugar and still a very light flavor. Used it on top of a homemade key lime pie which was tart, so the balance was good. Tip…after chilling bowl/whisk for 10min, I put ice packs under the mixing bowl to keep chilled while mixing. Worked like charm and it whipped up fast!

Turned out great, chilled my mixing bowl and beater also I made Fruity Pebbles Whip cream. I put 2 cups of heavy cream in a bowl of Fruity Pebbles and let it sit for a few minutes and then used cheese cloth to strain it out, out of the two cup I got about 1 cup back and added a second cup of just heavy cream to it.

Great recipe, althought I added a bit more sugar. If you want just one or two servings in a pinch to top ice cream, smoothies, or whatever, follow this recipe, but in a blender! Just leave it in until the blender appears to be going quite a bit slower. I suggest a Magic Bullet, they're cheap and freaking awesome!

I tried using my electric mixer, but it wasn't working. It just stayed runny, then I used the whisk instead of the blades and all was saved. Oh I also used a mom trick and had two metal bowls one larger with ice in it and set the mixing bowl in it. It worked great. I like it sweet so I added two equal packets and it did the trick, plus no added sugar.

Great recipe! I refrigerated the whisks and smaller metal bowl as well as the heavy whipping cream in the freezer for 20 minutes. I doubled the confectioner’s sugar. For flavoring, I sometimes use vanilla and other times lime juice etc. I used a metal bowl inside a larger metal bowl laden with ice to keep things very cold.

I love this whipped cream!! The only thing is that it isn't as sweet as I would like it. If you are the same way, I would add 1 tsp more powdered sugar and beat for another 10 seconds. It should be sweet enough after you do that.

It wasn't quite sweet enough, so I doubled the sugar to 2 Tbl powdered sugar. Otherwise, perfect. Just gotta know when to stop and when to whip more. The first time, It was kind of heavy. But that's because I didn't whip it quite enough.

I made it using Truvia because I do not like my whipped cream to be too sweet and it was so good. I used a ceramic bowl because I was too lazy to look for the metal one and chilled it with the whisk for 10 minutes. It was nice a fluffy and I saved some for the next day and made trifle with fresh strawberries and pound cake. It was tasty and fresh and I'm never buying store bought whipped cream again.?

Tasty tasty recipe. Chilled bowl and beaters like suggested and followed what others had said about adding more sugar. I only had powered sugar and as we are on stay at home orders, I went with what I had.
2 tbsp powdered sugar and 1 tsp vanilla. And like others have said "I never have to buy cool whip again." So, yummy and Im certain will go perfect with morning smoothies, banana splits, pies etc. Yum to the 10th factor
so easy! love this recipe and it tastes soooo much better than store bought.
Easy to make. I used my Magic Bullet. Worked really well. Delicious. Made for strawberry shortcake.
This homemade whipped cream was delicious but I made an adjustment. Add 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon of salt. That way it can balance out the sweetness. It was great thank you!

Needed a little more sugar for my taste...[1+1/2 - 2 Tbsp.] Update 1/27/26: Looking forward to experimenting with various flavors then possibly making a whipped pie in a chocolate pie shell. Debating on flavors to use. Just tried again using cocoa powder & mint extract. Needed a squirt of stevia to bring out more flavor. I encourage you to try the original recipe then start experimenting. So much fun for whipped cream fans.
Great Easy. No corn syrup or maltodextrin or whatever they're trying to sneak in now a days. Have used regular sugar also.
Easy and yummy
Made it with a hand whisk and was easy
loved it
Granddaughter made it…of course she double the sugar, lol. It was delicious though and whipped up in no time! I think I’ll try different flavorings next time.
